snippets.text: Rich Hickey, creator of Clojure, argues in a LinkedIn essay that LLMs are not tools but automation "with which you avoid writing code", and the post has 171 points on Hacker News.
snippets.why: A well-known language designer's case against calling LLMs tools is drawing a large debate among programmers on the day's Hacker News front page.

snippets.text: Artificial Analysis says Meta's Muse Wonder Full matches Claude Opus at xhigh effort on its index using fewer tokens, while the standard API Wonder scores below GPT-6.1 Sol, according to developer Theo.
snippets.why: Theo's reading of the chart suggests the two Wonder models behave quite differently, and the stronger one is limited to subscribers.

snippets.text: Meta's Alexandr Wang says a bug that burned Muse Wonder quota unusually fast is fixed, and Muse Code usage limits have been reset, in a post with a video and more than 1,500 likes.
snippets.why: It is the second usage reset this week from a lab, after OpenAI's Codex lead announced one, as coding-agent limits become a launch-week flashpoint.

snippets.text: An NVIDIA paper on LoGRA, a memory-saving method for reinforcement-learning post-training, reports 7.2 GiB of training memory at 1.5B parameters versus 13.2 GiB for rank-256 LoRA, as relayed by AI writer omarsar0.
snippets.why: If it holds up, full-weight RL on small models would fit on less GPU memory than adapter methods need, though the figures come from the authors.

snippets.text: Work2Skill, a paper from Shanghai Jiao Tong, Fudan and other universities, turns recorded human GUI demonstrations into reusable skills for computer-use agents, lifting GPT-5.5 to 48.44% on MyPCBench against 37.50% for baselines.
snippets.why: Code is on GitHub, and the result suggests agents can learn desktop workflows from watching people, not only from written instructions.

snippets.text: Wired reports that X users punked Elon Musk after he bragged about his Grok Lego Star Wars haul.
snippets.why: Only Wired has the story so far, and Musk's reply was not in the material seen; it is a small, odd moment for Grok.

snippets.text: Reuters reports Japan's Omron will buy US industrial PC maker OnLogic and its parent Interlogic for $675 million, the company said on Tuesday, to push into what it calls physical AI.
snippets.why: Rugged factory-floor computers are the hardware layer physical AI runs on, so the deal shows automation firms buying compute rather than building it.

snippets.text: A PhotonCap summary of AMD's OCP keynote says Lisa Su introduced a 6th Gen EPYC "Verano" CPU with an LPDDR memory interface, available in 2027, alongside a Helion agentic-AI rack.
snippets.why: LPDDR on a server CPU targets the memory demands of agent workloads; the details come from a second-hand summary, not AMD's own release.

snippets.text: Intel's product page for the D270 inference card lists up to 480 GB of LPDDR5X, 350 W air cooling and a PCIe 5.0 form factor, with no shipping date and no performance figures.
snippets.why: Trading HBM for cheap high-capacity LPDDR is Intel's bet that long-context inference needs memory size more than raw bandwidth.

snippets.text: StockSavvyShay says Meta is adopting Nvidia Spectrum-6 switches for its Vera Rubin AI factories, using its own open-source software to connect more than 100,000 GPUs with fewer networking layers.
snippets.why: It shows Nvidia selling networking to Meta even as Meta builds its own MTIA chips; the claim comes from an investor account, not Meta.

snippets.text: Hesamation quotes an Anthropic report saying requests to Moonshot's Kimi models were secretly forwarded to Claude, including one from a suspected People's Liberation Army-linked user analysing CCTV footage of a person.
snippets.why: It is Anthropic's own account of a distillation case, and Moonshot has not been shown responding to it in the material seen.

snippets.text: Axios reports Suki, an AI ambient scribe for healthcare providers, raised a $90 million Series E led by Healthier Capital; a source told Axios it projects $60 million to $80 million in revenue this year.
snippets.why: Clinical note-taking is one of the few AI product categories with revenue already at scale, and the revenue figure is a single anonymous source's.
